citations.review_text: Not even 2 hours in and already found a way to softlock myself

I finished Fallen order 100% and so it was only natural for me to want to play Survivor. Unfortunately it seems like neither EA or Respawn wanted that to happen. 

66 minutes into my very first playthrough I'm encountering a bug that prevents me from doing a "force wall-run" on a jumping puzzle. What I've read the only solution is to start over. Ehh, it's not too bad, it's only an hour, but it isn't very reassuring after reading about the experiences other people have had and are having to this day. Few people say they've had no issues while many claim they lost saves and/or encountered bugs/glitches which made progression impossible.

claims.claim: Reviewers report issues with controller inputs failing or conflicting with keybindings and third-party launcher requirements.

citations.review_text:
What the hell is going on with this game. After playing through SW Jedi: Fallen Order this past week and being frustrated by game design decisions, but still enjoying a Star Wars story - I did not expect SW Jedi: Survivor to be an unfunctional sequel. 

Performance is consistently tanking - ymmv here but it's consistently stuttering/dropping frames. The load times on respawn/save are better then Fallen Order though. 

Controls - Once I unlocked the *first* new ability I had to stop playing. Why is that? Binding the controller input. There are so many actions that need to be bound, there is no way to map them all to a single controller. The development team worked around this by mapping multiple actions to a button. But there is no way for the player to map multiple actions to a single button - once you reassign a button, it breaks the default multiple action binding the button had. 

So I can choose to have either a force power, or a grappling hook, or another (unexplained) force power. 

Right now I am looking to the modding community to have any hope of continuing to play this game. There are multiple performance optimization mods, and one keybinding mod. Since the development team decided to store keybindings in a binary file rather than a config file humans could edit.

Looking forward to all the
`ActionName="ForcePush",bShift=False,bCtrl=False,bAlt=False,bCmd=False,Key=Gamepad_RightTrigger`
nonsense so I can get through the game intro.

Game play was fun at first. However, controller stopped working completely in game after 1 hour, works fine in steam. Did some searching, seems to be a long-standing bug caused by the crappy EA launcher, there are some work around which I'm too lazy to try out each of them. Had to refund because I did't want to play the rest of the game using keyboard and mouse. Seriously EA, the bug report dated back years ago and I'm still experiencing it! Fixed your sh*t!

Between the keyboard key unregistering  or just not working even though its binded to a key, it feels like those generic Unreal5 game that are coming out by the dozen where the key layout if flat out unsuable. I have been spending the past hour working my way into rebinding everything and it seems that there are some keys that you flat out cannot rebind out of a controller and i dont own one. Only reason im not refunding is its on sale so i paid 18$ for it.

claims.claim: Reviewers report severe performance problems including stuttering, massive frame rate drops, and poor asset rendering in open areas.

citations.review_text:
Most of the good things about this game for me mostly revolve around existing mechanic upgrades. I'm enjoying the story all over again too after completing it on my Xbox.

Pros: 
- Cal's character is less boring that Fallen Order
- Fast travel 
- Less linear maps like Koboh for example
- 2 new lightsaber stances 
- Blaster!!!! 
- The game looks like an actual visual upgrade over Jedi: Fallen Order
- More customisation options for Cal and BD-1
- New enemies

Cons: 
- Massive FPS drops in certain parts of Koboh 
- I don't really like the 2 new lightsaber stances. I use single and dual blade stances and that gets me by.

Great game, Really good storytelling.
I loved this sequel to fallen order, the variations with the new styles are cool, The quality is nice.
I liked how much variety there is in customization, BD-1, Cal, Lightsaber parts, materials. The combat is good, You can fit into your own combat style if you can find one or two that you like. The quality is perfect (For me).
The only problems I have with this game are the frame drops. Whenever I load into a new area, it feels like so long before my frames go back to normal. Probably just me, my textures also broke because of this, requiring a restart of the game.
But, overall I would say if you can get good performance + Immersion, it's worth it, I'd say.

I like the game starts you right where the prequel ended in terms of character abilities, which makes you feel the development of Kal. Combat feels alright, nothing special. The gameplay loop favoured more puzzles and platforming rather than exploration, sneaking around or combat encounters. Unfortunately the storytelling is rather llinear which takes away from the enjoyment a bit too. Some of the story moments also felt a bit off from the Star Wars spirit we expect. My biggest disappointment was the performance especially on open areas where i went from "okay, whatever" to underwhelming. My PC ain't no monster but it is chunky considering the game's release date. Given the hype, the story, the subpar gameplay loop and the perfomance, I cannot recommend the game at 60 bucks. On a big discount it is a good one if you like an average souls-like in a star wars setting.

P. S. EA, gimme 10 bucks and this will become a positive review ;}

citations.review_text:
First off, you can't even play the game unless you create an EA account and install the app on your PC. It puts you in a bad mood immediately because it takes almost 15 minutes just to get into actually playing the game.
So now, being in a bad mood, people are going to be extra critical of any issues in the gameplay. It was not difficult to find issues right away. 
Simply trying to run this game on high settings was bad. For such a small beginning level, it was using all 30 gigs of my RAM and 15 gigs of VRAM, which could barely get 50 FPS. The environment didn't even have breakable objects (except for 2 spots) which shows how little effort the developers put into it. Why did this game run so bad for the tiny first level? The first level should hook you and show you how many interesting mechanics are involved in the game, but it was severely lacking in any content. Back when I played Force Unleashed, it was great. I could do so many things and engage with every enemy and object in the environment.
I had another issue with the movement of the character. It's very floaty and not snappy at all. It can barely be described as an action game. 
There's a reason why this game is often on sale for $10. It's not optimized and clearly lacking in many ways.

In terms of sequels, I think SWJS is one of the best products in gaming industry. Ofc optimisation sucks in this one, but I followed a few guides and managed to achieve 70-100 fps with very rare stutters – game was perfectly playable. It's a great follow-up with many upgrades and it lacks your usual "sequel amnesia" of main character.

Star Wars vibes, visuals, music, metroidvania implementation, gameplay and overall flow – perfect! I kinda couldn't understand or time majority of parries and I sucked for it, but still finished it on medium difficulty. My biggest gripe with this game is that there is not that many planets we visit, I would have loved to travel to 2-3 more. But the vastness of the ones available totally makes up for it.

I absolutely loved "low treat level" enemies' dialogues and monologues and I always hesitated with attack, just to hear 100% of it. That's peak SW humor, and for that Jedi Survivor will always be very close to my heart.

In the end I wanted to add that Turgle is just too cute and innocent.

A Great sequel to Jedi: Fallen Order, however, performance still remains the core issue, there are specific areas in the game where the frame rates drop significantly. It's been quite some time since the launch, and these issues should have been addressed by now. 

As for the story, the prequel had a great narrative, this one comes close to it. It continues from the last part with a little time gap. 

The gameplay is really improved and expanded, with new the force abilities, lightsaber combat, new stances, crazy stuff to try out, the puzzles, though, are a bit bewildering and might require some guide look-ups.

All in all, a solid 8/10, though, I really hoped they would've improved the performance.

I love this game, so, so much! Imo, it is a perfect sequel. The characters are more developed, the story is fantastic, the combat is much better (Cal climbs faster, traversal is more fun, etc), and even more customization! 

The one thing that is not perfect, however, is the performance probelms. EA clearly did not optimize this game for PC and theres a lot of crashes. I don't have the latest and greatest specs obviously, but I meet the requirements. Recently, I've been having more problems with crashing, and I don't know why. I had to turn all of my graphics settings to low when they worked fine on medium before. Textures take a long time to load. There have been a couple times now where my computer has completely crashed while playing. I couldn't Alt+Tab out to close it, I could bring up task manager with a keyboard shortcut, but then couldn't bring it to overlay on top of the game, so I couldn't access it. so I had to Ctrl+Alt+Del and shut down my computer while the game was still running. Maybe on better specs it runs better, but I have heard people who have a more advanced set up than I do still say they have these types of problems, so I don't know. 

It sucks bc this is one of my favourite games of all time, and it's so fun when it's working properly. But because of the technical issues, I would definitely say to wait to get it on sale bc the crashing makes it not worth it full price. BUT all that being said, I do still recommend it because the story is just THAT good.

STAR WARS Jedi: Survivor takes everything that worked in Fallen Order and expands it into a much larger and more ambitious experience. Bigger environments, more combat styles, more exploration, more progression systems, and a story that feels significantly more emotional and mature than the first game.

The strongest aspect of the game is easily its narrative and atmosphere. The story evolves naturally from Fallen Order and manages to keep that same sense of tension, betrayal, fear, and emotional weight that made the previous game memorable. Cal’s journey feels more personal this time, and the ending leaves a strong setup for the future of the franchise.

Visually, the game is beautiful. The environments, lighting, facial animations, and overall presentation are a clear improvement over the first game. Some moments genuinely feel cinematic in the best possible way, especially during larger story sequences and character interactions.

However, the technical state of the game continues to be its biggest problem. Even years after launch, performance issues are still very noticeable. Stutters, unstable frametimes, texture pop-in, visual bugs, lighting glitches, geometry issues, and inconsistent optimization remain present throughout the experience. Some areas perform normally, while others suddenly suffer from heavy FPS drops for no clear reason. This becomes especially frustrating during exploration or combat-heavy moments.

The combat system also feels like it hasn’t evolved as much as it should have. There is more variety now, with different stances and expanded skill trees, but the core structure still relies too heavily on dodge, parry, animation timing, and Souls-like mechanics. Personally, I think Star Wars should lean more into dynamic Jedi combat rather than trying so hard to imitate a Souls formula.

The Force itself feels too limited during gameplay. In the movies and series, Jedi constantly manipulate the environment around them, but here most inte…

The worlds are incredibly detailed and there is a ton of lore that comes from side quests, as well as other in game locations. I love the small details scattered across the worlds. It seriously feels like I am in the world at times and I couldn't ask for better immersion. The story is also incredibly good, and I would argue that it is easily on par or better than the first game. 

Pros:
-Immersive
-Open World
-Tons of Star Wars Lore
-Incredible Story
Cons:
-Weak Optimization (Way better than day one)
-Weird Graphical Bugs Sometimes
-Progression is Weird at Times

I love this game, so, so much! Imo, it is a perfect sequel. The characters are more developed, the story is fantastic, the combat is much better (Cal climbs faster, traversal is more fun, etc), and even more customization! 

The one thing that is not perfect, however, is the performance probelms. EA clearly did not optimize this game for PC and theres a lot of crashes. I don't have the latest and greatest specs obviously, but I meet the requirements. Recently, I've been having more problems with crashing, and I don't know why. I had to turn all of my graphics settings to low when they worked fine on medium before. Textures take a long time to load. There have been a couple times now where my computer has completely crashed while playing. I couldn't Alt+Tab out to close it, I could bring up task manager with a keyboard shortcut, but then couldn't bring it to overlay on top of the game, so I couldn't access it. so I had to Ctrl+Alt+Del and shut down my computer while the game was still running. Maybe on better specs it runs better, but I have heard people who have a more advanced set up than I do still say they have these types of problems, so I don't know. 

It sucks bc this is one of my favourite games of all time, and it's so fun when it's working properly. But because of the technical issues, I would definitely say to wait to get it on sale bc the crashing makes it not worth it full price. BUT all that being said, I do still recommend it because the story is just THAT good.

I really enjoyed Star Wars Jedi: Survivor. It improves on Fallen Order in almost every way, with fun exploration, satisfying combat, and a story that kept me invested in Cal’s journey. Overall, I had a great experience, but there are a few things I hope Respawn improves in the next game.

My biggest criticism is that the main story felt a little short. I found myself wanting more time with the characters and the overall narrative because I was enjoying it so much.

I also came across a few visual and animation issues that broke my immersion. For example, Mosey’s arm clips through her chest during one of her stretching animations, Cal’s lightsaber can clip through his clothing, one Jawa never rendered properly during my playthrough, and in one Force Echo only Dagan’s flowing hair is visible while the character speaking is missing. None of these issues ruined the game for me, but they made it feel less polished than it could have been.

One feature I really missed was a more immersive lightsaber customization system. Instead of simply choosing a blade color from a menu, I’d love to see each blade’s color tied to individual kyber crystals. It would make customization feel more meaningful and closer to Star Wars lore.

Finally, I’d love to see the combat system evolve by letting Cal learn and master different lightsaber forms independently of the stance he’s using. Rather than having the equipped stance completely define his fighting style, players could develop Cal’s mastery over different forms and combine them with their preferred lightsaber configuration. I think that would add more depth to combat while making Cal’s progression as a Jedi feel even more rewarding.

Despite these criticisms, I genuinely loved my time with Jedi: Survivor. It’s an excellent sequel that builds on the strengths of Fallen Order, and I’m excited to see where Respawn takes Cal’s story next.

I avoided this title for quite a while because so many reviews spoke about how broken of a port this game is. I'm not entirely sure if it was just dumb luck, or if they fixed the problems, but it really ran quite well for me. There were a few visual bugs like nothing more than floating hair delivering dialogue, weird shadows, misaligned objects in character's hands, etc, and the only game breaking bug I encountered (couldn't attack) only happened once and was fixed with a restart.

As for the game/story itself, I enjoyed many of the individual aspects and ideas of the game but it wasn't as tight narratively as the previous title. With a more open world, and a lack of strong character motivation for the early part of the game, I didn't feel quite as engaged with the story. 

I felt that the combat and encounter difficulty was pretty inconsistent, but I played on a harder difficulty so your milage may vary.

Still, overall these are just minor gripes, it was pretty enjoyable, good to grab on a sale if you played and enjoyed the first game.

I should also note that this game does require the EA launcher to run in the background, which can be a PITA.

Right so theres two reasons i give this a negative review, even though i got all achievos and put in this many hours. 
Reason 1, the state this game launched in. Now after many, many and i mean many patches, and some new hardware on my end, i could run this on max with almost no problems. However that doesnt excuse its terrible launch.
Reason 2, ea launcher, hate it. That is all.
Now the positive things. This game proves a jedi academy style rpg would work quite well, if only ea didn't controll the reigns for star wars.......

Although it's a fun game at times the story wasn't the best for me. Also the exploration that had you constantly going back and forth because you dont have certain abilities at times. The combat wasn't difficult but the way the game wanted to make it difficult was to throw as many enemies as possible with unblockable attacks (also oggdo bogdo). And last but not least the game obligates you to download EA account with is always a minus.

Game is, overall, fun to play. Major issues like game breaking bugs and extremely poor optimization rear their ugly heads, however. And since these issues are still present over 3 years after launch, it appears EA has no interest in fixing them. Which is a shame because there's a great game underneath all the frustrations.

Speaking of EA, another reason to boycott this is EA's awful app that you have to install to run the game. Why the ♥♥♥♥ am I getting pop up ads from a "legitimate" app? Apparently these mega companies don't make enough money so they want to usher the return of the early 2000's popup nightmare internet so they can squeeze even more money out of you. This is remedied easily by uninstalling the app or disabling it on startup, but the fact that ads like that are even present is just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ embarrassing.

The best things for me were the insanely good graphics, sound design that stayed true to Star Wars, satisfying combat, and a good story. The game also did justice to Darth Vader's appearance, though I wish there had been more of him.

The things I hated were the excessive traversal puzzles. I spent a huge chunk of time trying to figure out where to go. Holomap design didn't help much. Another big disappointment was that weapon stances can only be changed at meditation points instead of during combat. PC optimization is trash. Even on the lowest settings, the game couldn't give me 60 FPS, yet I was getting a stable 30 FPS on high to ultra settings dkw. Ending was unsatisfying.

I enjoyed *Jedi: Fallen Order*, and I loved this game as well. Overall, I'd give it an 8.2/10.

Recommended but with some caveats.

This game is a lot like the first, which I liked. You're playing as Cal Kestis, one of the last surviving Jedi. You find old allies and make new friends and fight with your light saber in a variety of possible stances. You go through the maps on each planet, slowly finding new areas and unlocking shortcuts as you get new abilities. You can also customize Cal's appearance and light saber with items you find along the way, but I have to admit I don't really care about that.

The caveats? First, the puzzles are more annoying than they were in the first game and the levels are excessively convoluted. I usually don't bother with walkthroughs--figuring things out is part of the fun of most games--but more than once I found myself on youtube trying to get a hint on some stupid puzzle or figure out what wall I need to be jumping off of next. 

It doesn't help that the map and navigation assistance aren't very good. You have to zoom in to see anything, and the path that you need to take through any given level is so ridiculously complex that it would be hard to follow on a better map.

Second, the platforming seems excessive to me. I mean, I'm kind of tired of having to do a double jump and then use the grapple hook so I can wall run and then jump onto a pole before I swing towards a rope which I have to do a force pull to grab onto before swinging and doing a dash jump to get through a force field to finally land on a wall. It frankly gets to be kind of tedious.

 I will happily admit that this is not my favorite part of the game. I'd prefer the light saber to be the meat of the game, and it's really not. There were admittedly a few moments in the first game (the final escape, if I remember correctly, where you're wall running off of flying wreckage) where I thought the platforming got to be too much, but they seemed to have leaned into it.
